page_title: DockFlip: the best bits of Windows, on your Mac

sources.entry: DockFlip - Dock window lists with browser tabs, a Flip 3D ⌘Tab window switcher and Windows-style snapping in one app. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/geezery/DockFlip)

summary.name: DockFlip
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source macOS app that adds Windows-style window lists to the Dock, an Alt-Tab-like Flip 3D window switcher, and edge/corner window snapping.
keywords: mac window switcher without screen recording
use_cases: Switching between many open windows on a Mac like on Windows
Jumping to a specific browser tab from the Dock
Snapping windows to halves, quarters or maximized on macOS
Filtering open windows by typing a name after Cmd+Tab
Restoring window positions after unplugging an external display
summary.what_it_does: DockFlip shows a list of an app's windows when you hover its Dock icon, and lists browser tabs for browsers such as Safari, Chrome, Edge and Firefox. Holding Cmd and pressing Tab opens a slanted 3D stack of all windows, including minimized, full-screen and other-desktop windows, with type-to-filter search. Keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+Option plus arrows) snap windows to halves, maximize, or quarters, and dragging a window to an edge or corner also snaps it. The page says it uses only the Accessibility permission and draws its UI from data macOS already shares, so it does not need screen recording; it states it has no networking code, analytics or update pings.
notable: Browser tab listing in Dock hover previews
Uses Accessibility permission only, no screen recording
Free and open source, with a DockFlip for IT package and profile for teams
caveats: Requires a manual workaround to open the unsigned app: macOS warns it can't check the app, so the user must choose Open Anyway in Privacy & Security settings
Optional donations via GitHub; page says the app is free and stays free
